1.why: The system checks that the reset code belongs to the user by associating tokens with flow IDs and sessions.

2.why: The same reset code cannot work for any other user because tokens are tied to specific flow IDs and sessions.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated after a password reset (session.resetComplete = true clears the flow).

4.why: The website uses HTTPS with TLS (Bun.serve with cert/key files).

5.why: Reset codes are encrypted (randomValue uses crypto.getRandomValues) and user data is not exposed in logs/errors.

6.why: Email messages (mock) hide private user data; no real emails are sent, but the mock token is not tied to user data.

7.why: User-supplied data (email, passwords) is validated for length and syntax before processing.

8.why: Redirect links are only to the hospital’s site (no external URLs in the code).

9.why: Email templates (mock) contain no scripts or HTML from user input; the system uses text-only mock tokens.

10.why: Error pages and logs do not expose user’s private information or tokens (generic error messages).

11.why: Passwords are stored as Argon2id hashes, and no secrets are hardcoded in the source.

12.why: The system does not allow default credentials (sessions are randomly generated).

13.why: The system bars users after 5 MFA failures (session.mfaFailures >= 5 clears the flow).

14.why: The application does not reveal whether the username/email exists (generic response for all recovery requests).

15.why: Password reset codes are random (randomValue(32)), complex (hex), and user-specific (tied to flowId).
